title: ICA: Information-Aware Credit Assignment for Visually Grounded Long-Horizon Information-Seeking Agents

sections_read: Table 4; Table 5; B Additional Experimental Results (p.14)

rs.innovation_approach: 把完成轨迹中的可复用外部证据设为信用归因对象，按同题 rollout 中证据出现/未出现的终答成功率差排序，再将选中证据的二值奖励发给取得它的工具轮；终答独立监督。
rs.key_step: 稳定 URL 级证据身份 → 组内出现/未出现成功关联 Δe → 每种工具选正分 top 10% → turn-local binary reward → 分工具/终答标准化优势。
rs.why_non_obvious: 不是估计相同前缀的动作值；用低额外推理成本的跨完整轨迹关联替代逐步标签，并把弱连续估计只用于排名，避免直接用其幅值作奖励。
rs.trigger_condition: When repeated rollouts revisit identifiable external information and have mixed terminal outcomes, apply occurrence-conditioned success ranking and separate turn rewards to achieve denser evidence-acquisition supervision.
rs.acceptance_signal: low_evidence: manifest decision is null; no review payload was supplied or found in the local manifest/candidate/inventory lookup.
rs.abstract_strategy: Give reusable acquired items stable identities, rank them by their association with success, and supervise acquiring steps separately from terminal decisions.
rs.abstract_key_step: Convert conditional outcome differences into positive top-ranked membership, then normalize intermediate and terminal signals in separate scopes.
rs.abstract_why_non_obvious: Use retrospective cross-sequence association to manufacture missing intermediate supervision without treating its magnitude as a reliable local action value.
rs.abstract_trigger_condition: When comparable items recur across sequences with mixed outcomes, route selected-item membership to acquisition steps while reserving a fixed share of optimization weight for terminal decisions.

signatures.object: tool-acquired atomic evidence within one prompt rollout group
signatures.information: Completed old-policy trajectories, binary judged final outcomes, and occurrence of stable URL-level SEARCH entries / FETCH snapshots. No shared-prefix continuations, no fixed-state action alternatives, no do-intervention, no direct observation of causal necessity.
signatures.operation: Estimate P(success|acquired e) minus P(success|not acquired e), rank separately by tool type, select positive top fraction, and reward each tool turn whose returned evidence intersects the selected set.
signatures.output: Binary per-tool-turn reward; corresponding within-tool-type standardized advantage replacing uniform terminal outcome credit.
signatures.claimed_effect: Author-reported Table 2: on Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking, ICA-Snapshot versus GSPO-Snapshot gives BC-100 25.0 vs 22.0, GAIA 69.9 vs 60.2, XDS 71.0 vs 68.0, Seal-0 25.2 vs 24.3 Pass@1 (%). This compares the ICA package, not this sub-operation alone.

limitations.text: Author limitation: raw visual tokens still create redundancy/compute cost. No learned visual compression or pooling before tokenization; image resizing in A.3 is nevertheless performed.
limitations.quote: it inevitably introduces considerable token redundancy and computational overhead, particularly when processing visually dense or exceedingly long webpages.

limitations.text: Author limitation: no sophisticated context management for unbounded exploration; truncation can lose early evidence.
limitations.quote: In such cases of context overﬂow, the trajectory must be forcefully truncated, which may lead to the loss of early-retrieved crucial evidence

question.observed_failure: Outcome-only GSPO-Snapshot achieves 22.0/60.2/68.0/24.3 Pass@1 versus ICA 25.0/69.9/71.0/25.2 (Table 2); text SFT hits context overflow 36.0% on BC-100 and 20.0% Seal-0 under Table 3 limits. These are baseline outcomes/representation failures, not numerical proof of misassigned tool credit.
question.load_bearing_assumption: Uniform terminal credit treats intermediate acquisition actions alike; text-derived observations are assumed sufficiently stable and complete for evidence comparison.
question.scope: Qwen3-VL-8B/30B-A3B web SEARCH/FETCH/ANSWER agents with recurring source-level evidence and long trajectories.
question.success_criterion: Reported Pass@1 gains over fixed-snapshot GSPO; top-ranked evidence more sufficient for answering than random/tail at matched selection fraction and length bucket; reduced representation overflow.
question.why_open: Prior dense signals compare turns/states/answer probabilities without attributing outcomes to identifiable acquired evidence; parsing/truncation/summarization obscure recurring unit identity.

objective.signal_routing: All generated tokens of a SEARCH/FETCH turn inherit its evidence-membership advantage; all tokens of ANSWER get its shaped-terminal advantage. This is tool-turn advantage replacement, not addition of Δ to terminal reward, and not only an action-tag mask. Returned observations are conditioning information. A turn may get positive acquisition credit despite its trajectory failing. Eq.17 averages token log-ratios within each turn, Eq.19 averages tool turns separately and reserves w=.3 for final answer. Algorithm 1 line12–13 uses E_i (whole trajectory) instead of Eq.14 E_t^i; record follows explicit turn-local Eq.14 and flags code semantics unverified.
objective.normalization: per-channel mean+std: SEARCH-turn rewards across all SEARCH turns in group, FETCH likewise; shaped terminal rewards across trajectories. Algorithm 1 adds epsilon; value unreported. Not leave-one-out; sample contributes to its own evidence statistic and baseline.
objective.invariance: No optimal-policy invariance theorem. Association-selected binary tool reward, terminal length shaping, independent normalization, and fixed answer/tool weighting alter the surrogate; not gamma Phi(s_next)-Phi(s) PBRS. Positive affine scaling within one nonconstant channel is approximately removed by std (epsilon aside); scale w outside normalization remains influential. Holding success fixed, longer failures are penalized less, so objective is not minimal necessary calls.
objective.baseline_or_potential: Empirical group means over post-hoc rewards, no critic/potential. Δ uses completed trajectories from pi_old and final judged correctness, not prefix success MC, not Q^{current}(h,a), not frozen reader before/after, not same-state counterfactual. Model-generated evidence occurrence determines association; reference judge accuracy is a separate issue.
objective.degenerate_cases: Author rule: all-success/all-failure groups set ALL TOOL advantages to zero. All-success final rewards identical => zero answer advantage with Algorithm1 epsilon. All-failure terminal rewards can vary with consumed length => nonzero final-answer advantage favoring longer failures (inference from Eq15–16), unlike tool channel. If either occurrence denominator zero, stated fallback sets P+ = P- = batch mean => Δ=0. No selected positive evidence or identical tool rewards => zero normalized tool signal with epsilon. Evidence acquired in all trajectories gets zero contrast. Unique evidence appearing only in one success can receive high Δ and overfit (inference). No forced sampling or policy-support repair for p(action)≈0/1. T_i=1 direct answer causes division by zero in Eq19 unless implementation special-cases; not specified. Repeated retrieval of selected evidence remains reward-eligible in Eq14; no first-acquisition-only condition.

evidence_design.discriminating_experiment: Table2 holds snapshot modality fixed for GSPO vs ICA; Table4 evaluates top/random/tail same-fraction evidence within five trajectory-length buckets (0–19 through 80–99). These discriminate acquisition-associated information sufficiency from some length confounding, but not same-state causal necessity or isolated components. Proposed unperformed falsifier: cross-fit evidence utilities, compare permuted/leave-one-out utilities, and match shaping/turn-ratio/answer-weight controls before interpreting credit mechanism.
controls: SFT-Text vs SFT-Snapshot (Table2), with raw text processing clarification in A.3 and mixed-modality SFT curation in A.4; identical teachers/data not established.
Fixed snapshot GSPO vs ICA (Table2); complete ICA bundle changes rewards, ratio granularity, and aggregation.
Top-p% versus random-p% versus tail-p% for p=10/15/20 in each step-length bucket (Figure3/Table4).
Same 128k context, 16k per-tool-response truncation for text/snapshot overflow analysis (Table3).
Table1 starred literature baselines are heterogeneous reported systems; Table5 Pass@4 must not be combined with main Pass@1.

negative_results.text: Snapshot representation still has token overhead and forced truncation risk; not a universal compactness guarantee.
negative_results.quote: our system currently lacks a sophisticated context management strategy to handle unbounded exploration.

negative_results.text: No numeric continuous-Δ reward ablation is provided; authors motivate binarization by collapse under small groups.
negative_results.quote: Instead of relying on association-based utility scores that easily collapse under small group sizes, we assign a binary reward
negative_results.locator: §4.1 p.5 Action-Turn Reward; author claim, not isolated experiment

evidence_design.seeds: Main training-run seed count and confidence intervals unreported (null, not assumed single). Appendix Table5/B says four random seeds for baseline evaluation and reports Pass@4; that is multi-sample success, not four independent training replications or seed-averaged Pass@1.
evidence_design.falsifier: For the transfer claim, if held-out evidence utility ranking is unstable or shuffled ranking gives equal improvement after matched shaping/normalization/compute, the evidence-aware mechanism interpretation fails; if it improves answer sufficiency while increasing crop counts, the fewer-necessary-crops transfer claim fails. These tests have not been run.

engineering.cost: Appendix A.2: 50 steps on NVIDIA H800, approximately 443 GPU-hours (8B) / 534 GPU-hours (30B-A3B). Training token count, updates-vs-rollouts breakdown, GPU count and incremental ICA cost versus GSPO not reported. 128k/16k are explicit diagnostic evaluation constraints, not inferred training limits.

pitfalls.text: Avoid tiny-group continuous utility reward magnitudes: authors rank and binarize; residual ranking noise remains.
pitfalls.quote: Instead of relying on association-based utility scores that easily collapse under small group sizes, we assign a binary reward

pitfalls.text: Long-page slices overlap to prevent severed lines/tables; coordinate identity alone is not enough to preserve readable evidence.
pitfalls.quote: vertical overlap 112 pixels, reducing boundary truncation artifacts

engineering.lesson: 当按完整轨迹中证据出现与成功的关联分配信用时，应先验证证据身份、组内出现/未出现支撑与独立排名稳定性，再检查 turn-local mask；否则唯一证据可能只是成功标签的代理、重复取证可被重复奖励，且正文 E_t^i 与伪代码 E_i 的差别会改变所有工具轮的信用。

relevance.how: 提供按取得证据分组的工具轮信用候选；但证据关联不是逐次必要性，不能关闭 P11。
工具轮替换式优势的直接近邻；独立标准化与长失败保护改变方向，未证明少裁。
不用冻结读者前后判分，但当前/旧策略整轨迹关联仍不等于当前状态所需信息。
失败轨迹可共享成功证据获工具正信用；全错组仍无工具信号，未区分合理失败与乱裁。
给取证工具轮所有生成 token 同一优势，提供明确而较粗的责任边界，caption-before-crop 需单独对齐。
复用同题已完成 rollout 的出现统计，不另开 MC 分叉；真实边际成本未报告。
